QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_58

question.text: A significant proportion of beneficiaries in the Niwas case are waste-pickers — an extremely vulnerable group. The SIA's evidence-collection plan should therefore:

answer.text: Use culturally sensitive interviews / questionnaires with Swagruha community workers present where needed, and acknowledge any internal data inconsistencies (such as 62% versus 50% waste-picker figures in different parts of the workbook) when citing those statistics

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook supports culturally sensitive engagement with vulnerable and informal-sector beneficiaries such as waste pickers, and notes that beneficiaries were not comfortable without the presence of Swagruha community workers. It also contains different waste-picker figures (62% on page 189 and 50% in the sample report on page 199), which the SIA should reconcile. The Trap: Standard surveys, postal forms and email-only surveys are inaccessible to many vulnerable beneficiaries. Note: Document the adaptations made for vulnerable groups and disclose any internal inconsistencies in the underlying statistics used.
